summary: Radar for 2026-11-25 (GLP-1 focus). Three things are new today. (1) An RSNA 2026 study, covered by Reuters, TODAY, NY Post and Medical News Today on 11-24/25, found breast density rose on mammograms in all 107 women who lost about 40 lb on a GLP-1 over a year or more. Callbacks followed, and all 4 biopsies were benign. It's at the early, emerging stage, women make up a big share of the audience, and few creators have covered it. It fits best as a calm 'Is this normal?' explainer: keep screening and tell your imaging team. (2) CBC reports a Health Canada vision-loss (NAION) warning for semaglutide, and Google Trends shows 'semaglutide' at 1,000+ searches in Canada today. This refreshes the FDA's 9 November class-wide NAION label change. Use it inside the held Serious Risks video, not as a news Short. (3) The Guardian reports oat sales soaring as 'nature's Ozempic'. That's a timely myth-correction hook for the 'natural GLP-1 support' pillar. Thanksgiving felt-symptom Shorts are at their peak for 11-26/27 only. On search-demand formats, Foundayo is still the strongest signal: there's a JAMA/AHA sleep apnea trial (ATTAIN-OSA) and an FDA filing is planned by end of 2026, so a ready Foundayo What to Expect video should ship now. Tirzepatide hair loss, nausea, pen use, after-6-months and stopping/keeping results stay evergreen. Medscape's 11-25 pieces on rechecking medications after weight loss and keeping weight off refresh the dizziness and stopping angles. Rejected: compounded-drug recalls and online price indexes, gray-market retatrutide seizures, the Tencent animal-study drug, and 'best online weight-loss services' listings.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 weight loss and mammograms: RSNA 2026 study found breast density rose in all 107 women who lost about 40 lb on a GLP-1, leading to some callbacks (4 biopsies, all benign)
candidates.angle: Calm 'Is this normal?' for women on tirzepatide or semaglutide: why losing breast fat can make tissue look denser on a mammogram, why a callback isn't a cancer signal, and the one thing to do: keep routine screening and tell your imaging team about GLP-1 use and recent weight loss. Small observational study; frame it as 'may', not a risk.
candidates.why_now: Presented at RSNA 2026 and picked up 11-24/25 by Reuters, TODAY, NY Post, Everyday Health and Medical News Today. Early mainstream coverage, little YouTube creator coverage yet. Women are a large share of the GLP-1 audience, and mammogram questions are a felt, practical moment.
